newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Family deny reports that Nigerian singer Fela dead.
newsitem.headline: Family deny reports that Nigerian singer Fela dead.

text.p: The family of Nigeria's maverick Afro-beat superstar Fela Anikulapo-Kuti on Thursday denied local media reports that he was dead.
"He is very much alive although he is really ill," said Funke Kuti, the wife of Fela's son, Femi Kuti.

"He is responding to treatment that he is being given," she told Reuters in response to conflicting reports in the Nigerian press that the musician, who has been critically ill for the past three weeks, had died.
Fears for the musician escalated on Wednesday when a private Lagos radio station reported that he had died earlier in the day.
The report was not repeated in subsequent news bulletins and journalists who thronged his Lagos home were unable to verify the report.
Funke said the radio station tendered an apology to the family on Thursday for the report.

A star of the Nigerian and international music scene in the 1970s and 1980s, the 58-year-old Anikulapo-Kuti, known to fans as "Fela" has a reputation for smoking marijuana, sleeping with large numbers of women and dressing only in underpants.
Since falling ill, Fela had been confined to his house in Lagos where he is cared for by an elder sister and a daughter. Numerous other women and hangers-on drift around the house.
On Monday, he was moved to what the Nigerian press called his "ancestral home" in Abeokuta, 80 km (50 miles) north of Lagos.
He had initially rejected both Western and traditional medicine but was now receiving treatment, his family said, but declined to say what medication he was taking.
